items.title: Marvel Studios Boss Suggests Kingpin Appearing in a Spider-Man Movie Isn't as Complicated as Fans Think
items.description: Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has given fans hope about the possibility of Kingpin showing up in a Spider-Man movie.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has given fans hope about the possibility of Kingpin showing up in a Spider-Man movie.

For years, some of our favorite Marvel characters have been wrapped up in complicated rights issues. Although Disney owns the bulk of the Marvel universe, there are some characters who are tied up elsewhere. Spider-Man's film rights are still owned by Sony, but are essentially loaned out to Marvel Studios for new live-action films and crossover events. The Hulk's solo films belong to Universal Pictures, which is why there hasn't been a new Hulk movie since 2008. And Kingpin is also apparently in some kind of legal purgatory.

Wilson Fisk actor Vincent D'Onofrio has expressed interest in playing the character in a Spider-Man film or even in his own spin-off movie, but has said it's not possible. In 2025, he claimed his character is only permitted to show up in TV shows.

"It's a very hard thing to do, for Marvel to use my character," said the Daredevil: Born Again actor. "It's a very hard thing to do, because of ownership and stuff. I’m only usable for television shows. Not even a one-off Wilson Fisk movie. It’s all caught up in rights and stuff. I don’t know when that would work out — or if it ever would work out at all.”

However, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige suggests it's not as big of a deal as people may think. When speaking with Josh Horowitz, Feige was asked whether or not Kingpin and Daredevil were ever considered for roles in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Feige downplayed D'Onofrio's concern over rights issues and stated that the characters were actually considered

"There are things to navigate like everything else," said Feige. "We talked about all those characters at one point."

Ultimately, it sounds like Feige could get the job done if the story demanded it. Will that ever happen? Who's to say! It would be awesome to see Fisk and Spidey duke it out on the big screen, though. However, Feige has managed to not only usher in Spider-Man into the MCU despite rights issues, but he also managed to bring the X-Men, Fantastic Four, and Daredevil into the MCU after years of rights issues and different ownership. Maybe Feige will work his magic for New York's notorious crime boss one day.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Kevin Feige 'Has Hope' That Spider-Man and Venom Will Finally Meet in the MCU
items.description: Marvel President Kevin Feige has said he’s holding out hope that Spider-Man and Venom will one day have their long-awaited crossover in the MCU.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige has said he’s holding out hope that Spider-Man and Venom will one day have their long-awaited crossover in the MCU.

Speaking to Josh Horowitz on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, Feige and film producer Amy Pascal chatted about the possibility of seeing the two characters finally meet up in a Marvel movie. While they didn’t say anything definitively, their remarks hinted that it’s something Marvel Studios is keenly aware of, though how realistic it actually is remains up in the air.

Horowitz asked the pair if they could reveal “how close” they’ve gotten to putting Tom Hardy’s Venom in a flick with Tom Holland’s Spider-Man, remarking that it’s been a major “bummer” the two haven’t had a single moment together after all these years.

“It would be great, let’s put it that way,” Pascal said diplomatically.

“Do you have hope?” Horowitz said, prompting Feige to vaguely answer, “We always have hope.”

“I have hope. We have hope,” Pascal playfully interjected.

While this answer, ironically, doesn’t give fans much hope that we’ll see these two versions of the characters share the screen anytime soon, Feige and Pascal did confirm that an animated Venom movie is still in the works.

News of this film first broke on February 23, 2026. Zach Lipovsky and Adam B. Stein, the duo behind Final Destination: Bloodlines, are set to direct the full-length feature, with names like Amy Pascal and even Tom Hardy himself said to be involved, though the exact nature of their relationship to the project is still unknown.

Plot details are also scarce, leaving fans anxious to know what adventure the Symbiote will go on next. Most are hopeful it’ll at least be a better experience than Venom: The Last Dance, which IGN’s Tom Jorgensen gave a 4 out of 10, citing its “boring, generic plot and bad action” that left audiences equal parts snoozing and confused at the cinema.

This is the latest news we’ve heard about a Spider-Man and Symbiote crossover after Tom Holland discussed the situation in response to a young fan during an interview for Brand New Day. “One day, I’m sure we’ll get to see the symbiote,” he said, though he admitted he couldn’t directly say whether or not it appears in the film.

The newest Spidey movie hits theaters on Friday, July 31. IGN scored the flick a 7 out of 10, saying it “effectively refocuses on the sturdiest pillars of the webslinger's iconography: struggling to find balance while swinging around New York City saving the day, and looking dang cool doing it.”

items.title: 'It Totally Didn't Work' - Tom Holland and Zendaya 'Hated' an Early Cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day
items.description: Tom Holland has revealed that he, Zendaya, and Jacob Batalon "hated" an early cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Tom Holland has revealed that he, Zendaya, and Jacob Batalon "hated" an early cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

When speaking with Quotable, Tom Holland was asked about what it feels like to finish such a massive film. He noted that he doesn't feel complete until the film has been out for a while and audiences have had a chance to respond to it, partially because a movie changes a lot from script to production to post-production. He went on to speak about how they watched a bunch of different cuts of the Brand New Day as part of this process, and the starring trio outright hated one of them.

"We've seen loads of different cuts of this movie, and one of the cuts, they took all of the notes from all of the random people who saw the film," said Holland. "And then they changed the movie, and we watched it, and we hated it. It totally didn't work. It was what the people were asking for, but it wasn't quite what we wanted as the creatives. But they learned lessons from that experience, so a movie can change in a thousand different ways in the edit room."

What Holland is seemingly speaking about is feedback from test screenings. Films will often show rough cuts to random audiences to gain feedback, but this has its pros and cons. One random audience can't always accurately predict how everyone will feel. Sometimes movies have been unintentionally butchered by test audiences who didn't understand it. It's up to the creative team to more or less decipher the underlying feedback that can actually help strengthen the project, as opposed to just taking it all at face value.

Luckily, it sounds as though the Spider-Man team was able to sift through the noise and make something that aligned with their vision while taking advantage of feedback. Spider-Man: Brand New Day currently boasts a 91% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and is tracking to have the biggest opening weekend of 2026. We gave the movie a 7/10, noting that it covers familiar ground for Spidey, but still managed to be an enjoyable adventure.

items.title: Yaga Showrunner Kat Sandler Talks Baba Yaga Being the 'OG Bad Girl of Fairytales'
items.author: Jessie Wade
items.content:
IGN spoke with the showrunner and executive producer of Yaga, Kat Sandler at San Diego Comic-Con, along with cast members Clark Backo and Noah Reid.

Yaga is based on the play by the same name created by Sandler, which is drawn from the Slavic folktale of Baba Yaga.

In speaking about what it was like bringing the story to the screen, Sandler said, "The fun thing about transitioning something from theater to film is you get to put so many more Easter eggs visually in it. You get to direct the eye with the camera to highlight lots of little tiny pieces and really build the mystery, build the sex, build the horniness by just being able to zero in on it a lot more, rather than just seeing one big picture of it."

When asked if the series has given Sandler interest in revisiting the play, she laughed, saying, "No, no. The play exists in its own thing, and it has now moved into something completely different with these wonderful, fabulous people (pointing to Reid and Backo) and Carrie-Anne and Hudson, and I can't wait to see where this version of it goes."

In terms of what drew Sandler to the tale of Baba Yaga to begin with, Sandler said, "she's always just been this incredible figure of wisdom and rage, and she's one of the only witches I think that has a name across all of these countries. She's such a big figure in Eastern European folklore, and she has this kind of very ambiguous moral code that was really resonant for me as someone looking to adapt things about female anti-heroes. I really grew up with Dexter and Hannibal and I was like, "can we do this but with a woman?' and still find it viciously entertaining and so fun and so sexy and really be along for the ride with her, enjoying her being the OG bad girl of fairytales."

Backo dug into her character, Detective Carson, explaining she's the practical one, and is very grounded and disciplined, while also intentionally focusing on protecting women.

"(She's) very skeptical of the case and this one (pointing to Reid). She believes deeply in the importance of her job as a cop to serve and protect. And I think she especially underlines protecting women, and understands the vulnerability in being a woman in this world – obviously because she is one herself – but also because its very apparant all around us that we live in a patricarchal society that does not lend well to the safety of women."

Even though Yaga has been described as a dark, mystery-thriller show, Reid and Backo spoke of the humor and comedy included as well, with the series sounding like a mash-up of multiple genres.

"I feel like this show really is a '90s detective movie wrapped in a pulpy rom-com with a dark, mythological thriller in it," Reid said. "I feel like the shift of that within the show is one of the things I love. And as a performer, one of the things I love so much is the switch of gears that way, from moments that feel like they are romantically-driven to comedy-driven to thriller/horror-driven."

Backo shared her thoughts saying, "I think the way that she (Sandler) blends all these genres together, especially using humor and comedy to be able to dive into extremely complicated, fragile, and complex themes – I think it just invites everybody to be able to pause and really think about, what does justice really look like? What does it look like when justice is served? Who are the monsters? What does good and evil really mean and look like?"

Backo added, "What she (Sandler) does so well, is keep it ambiguous, right until the end. And you kind of have to sit with yourself and decide 'what would you do?' in these peoples' positions."

For more on Yaga, check out the trailer reveal from San Diego Comic-Con and find out what Reid said about Hudson Williams joining the cast.

Jessie Wade is Associate Director of Editorial Programming at IGN. You can find her watching the latest rom-com and drama shows, reading a ridiculous amount of fiction books, and throwing herself into way too many hobbies.

items.title: Universal Studios Honors Ozzy Osbourne by Giving Him His Very Own Haunted House at Halloween Horror Nights
items.description: Universal Studios theme parks in Hollywood and Orlando are paying tribute to the late great Ozzy Osbourne, giving the ‘Prince of Darkness’ his very own haunted house at this year’s Halloween Horror Nights.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Universal Studios theme parks in Hollywood and Orlando are paying tribute to the late great Ozzy Osbourne, giving the ‘Prince of Darkness’ his very own haunted house at this year’s Halloween Horror Nights.

Fans of Ozzy Osbourne can take a ride on the Crazy Train through a spine-tingling journey featuring music from the metal icon’s prolific solo career this spooky season.

Described as a “living horror movie,” these completely original haunted houses are themed after Ozzy’s greatest solo hits, with songs from his post-Black Sabbath albums guiding guests through the chilling experience.

The ‘Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness’ houses are equal parts theme park attraction and a museum honoring his life and times, acting as a chronological trek through highlights of his discography with sets inspired by the iconic cover art of his most popular albums. Starting with ‘Crazy Train,’ park-goers will travel from dark dungeons and ancient ruins to Ozzy’s home in Birmingham, England, eventually finding themselves in the Osbourne Asylum, inspired by his album Diary of a Madman. They’ll also get treated to the singer’s various personas, including Madman Ozzy, Werewolf Ozzy, and, of course, The Prince of Darkness.

As per a press release from Universal Studios, the ‘Prince of Darkness’ haunted houses draw from the “heavier sound and sinister imagery that defined the later years of Ozzy’s career, transforming that creative evolution into a horrific journey through his unmistakably twisted imagination.”

Osbourne’s wife and son, Sharon and Jack Osbourne, gave Universal their blessing, calling the haunted houses a “wonderful tribute” to the legendary ‘Crazy Train’ singer.

"Ozzy never stopped pushing boundaries, and he loved anything that gave fans a new way to experience his music and the worlds he created," they expressed in a joint statement. "Halloween Horror Nights has done an incredible job bringing that spirit to life. Walking through these haunted houses, you'll recognize so many moments inspired by his music and imagination. It's a wonderful tribute to Ozzy, and we hope fans have as much fun experiencing it as he would have had seeing it come together."

“Ozzy Osbourne didn't just help define heavy metal — he created a cultural phenomenon that has influenced generations of music, art and horror,” John Murdy, Executive Producer of Halloween Horror Nights at Universal Studios Hollywood, added. “We previously had the privilege of collaborating with Ozzy, and this new haunted house is an opportunity to honor his extraordinary solo career. Inspired by all 13 of his albums, guests will journey through the dark, surreal worlds that fueled his music and cemented his legacy as the one and only Prince of Darkness.”

Halloween Horror Nights kicks off from Friday, August 28 through Sunday, November 1 at the Universal Orlando Resort. At Universal Studios Hollywood, it starts on Thursday, September 3 through Sunday, November 1. You can get your tickets for both theme parks right now on the official Halloween Horror Nights website.

Universal Studios is one of many brands who have paid tribute to Ozzy; following Osbourne's death in 2025, developer Double Fine honored the artist by making their heavy metal-themed game Brütal Legend free for just 666 minutes.

items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Director Is Pushing for a Physical Edition, But Nothing Has Been Decided
items.description: There's a chance that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation may not have a physical edition, but the director of the game is actively pushing to avoid that.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
There's a chance that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation may not have a physical edition, but the director of the game is actively pushing to avoid that.

When speaking with GamesRadar, director Naoki Hamaguchi was asked about the state of physical games and whether or not Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will receive a physical disc. Given the game is still almost a year away from release, Hamaguchi was unable to make any guarantees, but admitted that it is something important to him.

“We’re still having internal discussions on what the exact SKU product lineup is going to be for Revelation,” said Hamaguchi, “So, I can’t say anything particularly definitive at this point in time. But I am working to make the arrangements to allow us to have some kind of physical edition.”

He noted that platforms like Nintendo have certain rules, such as storage limits with things like game cartridges, which can make these decisions challenging. But ultimately, he hopes to have something that satisfies fans to the best of their ability.

"Each platform and first-party have their own specific rules and regulations that we need to take into account, and think about what format is actually going to be best for the game. These are the discussions that we're having at this point in time. I do hope that we'll be able to come up with something that is as close as possible as to what players and fans are going to want, but you'll have to look forward to future announcements for that."

He also joked that fans will "rip him to pieces" if the game doesn't have a physical edition following these comments. As for his personal feelings, Hamaguchi noted he is optimistic that there will always be some kind of physical item, even if it's just a code in the box or game key card, and values the ability to have a physical item commemorating the game that fans can cherish.

“I do feel, as a developer and as a fan, that the general trend is for things to shift away from physical towards downloadable games. But that’s obviously talking about the trend. Personally, here at something like Fan Fest or at community events for games that I’ve worked on, I really think that people bringing up things, asking for autographs. I think that’s lovely. I think it’s a wonderful culture and it would be a shame to lose that. I want that to remain.”

Although PlayStation's digital-only strategy won't begin until January 2028, almost a year after Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's release, that hasn't stopped some games from going all digital beforehand. Grand Theft Auto 6 will not release on a disc when it launches in November, and reports suggest there are no plans for that to change. items.title: Guillermo del Toro Says He Plays Angry Birds ‘Every Day’ of His Life
items.description: Speaking with IGN as part of our IGN30 Icon Series, Guillermo del Toro opened up about his favorite games — and while he gushed about many, one definitely stood out from the rest.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Speaking with IGN as part of our IGN30 Icon Series, Guillermo del Toro opened up about his favorite games — and while he gushed about many, one definitely stood out from the rest.

It’s no secret that Guillermo del Toro is a die-hard gamer. He’s spoken at length about his favorite titles, most recently retweeting a sculpture of Resident Evil 2’s Super Tyrant with an excited, “Aaaaah~.”

We got the chance to sit down with the acclaimed filmmaker at San Diego Comic Con 2026, where he celebrated the 20th anniversary of Pan's Labyrinth. During our chat, del Toro waxed poetic about the many games that have impacted him over the years, citing titles like Journey, Left 4 Dead, and Monument Valley.

“Death Stranding made me cry,” he told us. (It’s no surprise — he starred in the game, after all.) “Shadow of the Colossus made me introspective about so many intangible things. Bioshock, it’s a world I could get lost in for ages.”

However, his most surprising favorite doesn’t feature brooding themes or a dark, shadowy world. Instead, it’s one of the most popular mobile games of all time, notably featuring an iconic, upbeat theme song and bright, happy colors: Angry Birds.

“Every day of my life, every moment I have free, I’m still playing Angry Birds. I’m really good at it,” he admitted.

On the more predictable end of what you’d expect from del Toro’s tastes, he also revealed that he’s a massive fan of Dead Cells, though he jokingly asked the game’s developers to make a version without respawning for the older gamers out there.

“Dead Cells was really interesting to me,” he explained. “I just hate respawning, because you only get about 35 levels and then you start again. You get faster, but please, do a version without respawning for the older, for the elderly players. I’m available. Contact me and send it to me, please. I beg you!”

Our full, extended interview with Guillermo del Toro will be published later this year as part of the IGN30 Icons series. In the meantime, you can check out a previous episode of the series, where we chatted with Ken Levine, creator of famed games like System Shock 2 and its spiritual successor, Bioshock.

items.title: Yaga's Noah Reid Says People Will See 'A Different Side' to Hudson Williams in the Upcoming Series
items.author: Jessie Wade
items.content:
In an interview with IGN at San Diego Comic-Con, Yaga star Noah Reid shared what it was like working with Hudson Williams on the upcoming thriller series, based on showrunner Kat Sandler's Yaga play.

Reid said Williams joined the cast right as the craze of Heated Rivalry had fully kicked in, and they were all "really excited he was coming on board."

"When we found out Hudson was joining us on this show, Heated Rivalry fever was in full swing," Reid said. "The people love Hudson, there's no question."

Sandler chimed in saying, "And we love Hudson." To which, Reid responded, "Yeah, but that goes without saying, doesn't it?" Followed by laughter.

"This show I think will really highlight Hudson's ability as an actor," Reid continued. "He's a great actor and he's a cinephile, and he does his research, and people are going to see a different side of him in this show for sure."

Williams plays Henry Park, a young heir to a commercial fishery who goes missing, while Reid plays Rapp, a private investigator hired to find him.

Yaga is based on the Eastern European folktale of Baba Yaga, who is a witch with a complex moral code. She's been depicted throughout folklore as both the villain and the wise woman, with the upcoming series leaning towards more horror and sex in the story.

When asked how Sandler would describe the overall tone of her Yaga series, she said, "Propulsive, sexy, funny, dark, and wildly surprising."

Reid added some extra mystery for fans, saying, "There are so many twists and turns along the way; it really does keep you on your toes. In a half hour drama, things move very fast. It's jam-packed and if people aren't paying attention, they are gonna miss some stuff."

For our full interview with the Yaga crew, watch the video above, and read about Sandler going in depth about the series and how Baba Yaga is the "OG bad girl of fairytales."

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Modders Have Already Added Iron Man, Carl Johnson From GTA, and More
items.description: Halo: Campaign Evolved already has a bunch of mods, including one which replaces Master Chief with CJ from Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Halo: Campaign Evolved already has a bunch of mods, some of which are genuine quality-of-life upgrades, while others make silly additions, such as replacing Master Chief with Iron Man and CJ from Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

Halo: Campaign Evolved officially released earlier this week, and fans were quick to back all of its layers. Players swiftly discovered that the game has a secret ending, which seems to point to a remake of Halo 2. However, people are now using the foundation of Halo's Unreal Engine debut to mod the game to oblivion. Some of these mods are actually very helpful and make the game better, while others are, admittedly, very absurd.

For starters, Halo: Campaign Evolved has a mod where you can swap out the ever-stoic Master Chief for Carl Johnson, the protagonist from Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. It's sort of a rite of passage for games to have a playable CJ mod, as he's a very simple model to port between titles. It's also just very comical to see a regular man in a tank top and jeans running around fantastical environments, such as a sci-fi world where he can fight aliens.

Halo: Campaign Evolved also boasts a third-person POV if you find the right skull modifier for it, which would probably be the ideal way to experience this mod; otherwise, you'll only be able to see his hands in gameplay. Other mods also let you play as Iron Man, Brutes, and custom Spartans. There's a wealth of additional mods that change the gameplay experience as well, including visual overhauls that make the graphics even more realistic, downgrade it to PS1 visuals, and even one that adds a dynamic day/night cycle.

As for gameplay changes, some mods add weapons, tweak existing guns to be more like other Halo games, and there's even one that adds the jetpack from Halo: Reach. On consoles, players can play the game in split-screen, but that's not possible on PC... unless you download a mod that adds the feature in. Ultimately, there are already a lot of really fun ways to enhance the game on PC, and if you're looking to spice up this Halo remake, you should check out the game's page on NexusMods.

items.title: Xbox Promises to Investigate Reports of Service Outage Preventing Players From Accessing Physical Games
items.description: Xbox is soothing fans’ fears around digital ownership following a system-wide outage that reportedly prevented games on physical discs from being played without an internet connection.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Xbox is soothing fans’ fears around digital ownership following a system-wide outage that reportedly prevented games on physical discs from being played without an internet connection.

Speaking to The Verge, Xbox’s Chief Technology Officer Scott Van Vliet promised players that the company is investigating these reports, echoing the popular sentiment that, yes, games you own on a physical disc should work offline.

“We’re looking into reports that some players were unable to access games using discs as expected during the service interruption,” Vliet said. “Disc-based entitlement checks should not prevent players from accessing their games, and this is by design.”

The outage occurred late on Sunday night, July 26, and lasted well into the next day before finally being resolved late on July 27. The issue prevented players from logging into their Xbox accounts, viewing their game libraries, and even playing games at all. Vliet confirmed that this was due to "a licensing service that sits outside of Xbox, but which Xbox depends upon,” vowing to “do better” and calling the disruption an “unacceptable situation.”

“We're running a full post-incident review,” he said in a tweet. “I care less about the one-line root cause and more about the real questions: why a failure in one service was able to take down this much, why recovery took as long as it did, and what we change so a single point of failure can't ruin your night again.”

Xbox wasn’t the only major games network that suffered from an outage recently; PlayStation Network also went down for hours on the morning of July 24, preventing players from accessing digital games and launching apps, as well as throwing a major wrench into Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls's record-breaking open beta. Luckily, things were resolved that same day, though PlayStation has not publicly revealed the cause of the issue.

That being said, the PlayStation outage prompted a slew of posts from players hailing the benefits of physical games, which were largely untouched by the network disruption and still playable offline, in the wake of Sony’s decision to eventually end all production of physical game discs by January 2028.

Xbox, on the other hand, is reportedly preparing a method that would allow players to digitize their physical games, allowing them to stick the disc into and giving them a digital license for said game. What’s more, if a player gives or sells a disc to someone else, that digital license then follows its new owner, but the physical version will still work if players choose not to digitize it.

For now, the growing discontent around Sony’s decision to eschew physical discs in favor of a digital-only future continues to ruffle feathers, prompting players to flood the brand’s social media with comments protesting the plans and hoping some way, somehow, it'll change its mind.

items.title: Crunchyroll Announces First Streaming Bundle for U.S. Subscribers
items.description: Crunchyroll just announced its first streaming bundle, but you can only get it through Prime Video.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Crunchyroll just announced its first-ever streaming bundle for U.S. subscribers. The anime service is now available in a bundle with Starz for $16.99/month, but the bundle is only purchasable through Prime Video.

Crunchyroll offers three different plans through its own streaming website. Per Amazon's press release, the bundle offers a savings of 23%. That savings percentage suggests the bundle is based on the standard ‘Fan’ tier of Crunchyroll, which typically costs $9.99/mo. Starz, on the other hand, only has one standalone plan at $11.99/mo.

Prime Video’s Director of U.S. Channels, Matt Huntley, spoke on the somewhat unconventional combination of services coming to Amazon: “Whether it’s premium dramas, blockbuster films, or world-class anime, Prime Video is making it seamless for customers to access the entertainment they want, all in one place.”

Both services are also currently offering their own standalone deals. Starz is offering new subscribers three months at $5.99/mo, while Crunchyroll is knocking 17% off annual plans until the end of July. Two of the more niche streamers certainly seem to be making an aggressive push for subscriber growth.

Crunchyroll currently stands as the largest anime streaming service in North America, boasting over 21 million subscribers. Most major changes to the service have occurred since it was controversially acquired by and merged with Funimation back in 2021. Now, Crunchyroll is technically a joint venture between the U.S.-based Sony Pictures Entertainment and Japan’s Aniplex Inc., both of which are subsidiaries of Tokyo-based Sony Group.

Under the Sony banner, Crunchyroll has expanded its offerings beyond anime streaming. Crunchyroll Manga was rolled out late in 2025, and the service has been doubling down on getting new additions into its Crunchyroll Game Vault.

More recently, the service announced it will be restricting access to the Crunchyroll Store to subscribers of its most expensive subscription tiers. Given that the new streaming bundle seemingly combines the Fan tier and is also exclusive to Prime Video, it’s most likely that subscribers to this specific bundle will not get access to these other Crunchyroll services.

Other recent changes to Crunchyroll include the removal of its free ad-supported streaming tier at the end of last year, soon followed by a price hike that went into effect this past March. One thing the service surprisingly hasn’t gotten rid of is a seven-day free trial.

While this is the first Crunchroll streaming bundle available in the U.S., Starz is available in bundles with a number of other streaming services, including Hallmark+, HBO Max, and MGM+. The service last reported crossing over 17.6 million subscribers, and is home to original series like Outlander as well as new releases from Lionsgate Films and Universal Pictures.

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who, when she isn't following streaming news, spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

items.title: BioWare's Former Dragon Age Boss Says a Mass Effect-Style Remaster Trilogy Is Pretty Much Impossible
items.description: Don't hold your breath for remasters of the original Dragon Age trilogy - they're pretty much impossible, BioWare's former Dragon Age boss has said.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Don't hold your breath for remasters of the original Dragon Age trilogy - they're pretty much impossible, BioWare's former Dragon Age boss has said.

In an interview with FRVR, ex-Dragon Age series producer Mark Darrah was asked about the chances of a remastered collection of the first three Dragon Age games, similar to the Mass Effect collection. He noted that while he had previously envisioned a "Champion's Trilogy" that would attempt to unify all three games (since they're quite different from each other), he doesn't think it's likely anymore.

Why? Because no one currently at BioWare understands the engine those games were built on, and as a result, it also can't be outsourced because all that institutional knowledge is gone.

“There is basically no one at BioWare anymore that understands the Aurora Engine,” Darrah claimed. “There’s basically no one outside of BioWare anymore that understands the Aurora engine. So unlike Mass Effect, which is Unreal… there are basically no companies that could help you.”

Dragon Age began life in 2009 with the much-loved Dragon Age: Origins, and was quickly followed-up by Dragon Age 2 just two years later. The hugely successful Dragon Age: Inquisition came out in 2014.

Darrah noted that the only way a Dragon Age Trilogy remaster might be feasible is if EA built an entire team with this project in mind, but that would ultimately mean they aren't working on other new projects, which isn't as savory for a big publisher like EA.

Darrah had previously noted that EA isn't a big fan of remasters either, which is mostly evident in its library of titles. The Mass Effect trilogy and the remake of Dead Space are exceptions, but fans have been clamoring for revivals of other games like Dragon Age, Need for Speed, and more.

Maybe one day a Dragon Age collection will come to fruition, but it doesn't sound like it would happen anytime soon. It doesn't help that Dragon Age: The Veilguard flopped as well, which may have soured EA on doing anything with the IP for the foreseeable future.

“There is basically no one at BioWare anymore that understands the Aurora Engine,” Darrah claimed. “There’s basically no one outside of BioWare anymore that understands the Aurora engine. So unlike Mass Effect, which is Unreal… there are basically no companies that could help you.”

Dragon Age began life in 2009 with the much-loved Dragon Age: Origins, and was quickly followed-up by Dragon Age 2 just two years later. The hugely successful Dragon Age: Inquisition came out in 2014.

Darrah noted that the only way a Dragon Age Trilogy remaster might be feasible is if EA built an entire team with this project in mind, but that would ultimately mean they aren't working on other new projects, which isn't as savory for a big publisher like EA.

Darrah had previously noted that EA isn't a big fan of remasters either, which is mostly evident in its library of titles. The Mass Effect trilogy and the remake of Dead Space are exceptions, but fans have been clamoring for revivals of other games like Dragon Age, Need for Speed, and more.

items.title: Makoto Shinkai’s Your Name Returning to Theaters in New 4K Remaster
items.description: Writer-director Makoto Shinkai’s beloved 2016 anime film Your Name has been remastered in 4K for a North American theatrical re-release next month.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Writer-director Makoto Shinkai’s beloved 2016 anime film Your Name has been remastered in 4K for a North American theatrical re-release next month.

GKIDS will release the 4K remaster of Your Name in theaters nationwide starting August 14 in both its original Japanese language and English dub versions. IGN can exclusively reveal the trailer for the re-release, which can be watched via the player below.

Animated by CoMix Wave Films, Your Name became a global phenomenon upon its release in 2016. With a worldwide box office haul north of $400 million, Your Name remains the highest-grossing original Japanese animated feature of all time.

Described by GKIDS in their official announcement as “a breathtaking love story across time,” Your Name follows “rural schoolgirl Mitsuha and city kid Taki [who] awaken to discover that they’ve switched bodies. The total strangers struggle to navigate each other’s lives, walking tightropes of intimacy and distance. But when they finally resolve to meet, the true nature of their connection threatens to seal their fate.”

In her Your Name review, IGN’s critic Jenna Busch wrote “the animation is absolutely gorgeous and the story will grab your heart and squeeze. Your Name doesn’t quite match the feel of a classic Miyazaki film, but it’s still a lovely story that actually manages to make the time travel mostly understandable… This is definitely worth a watch.”

For more anime coverage, check out our picks for the best new anime to watch this summer, best anime series of all time, and our ranking of the best Studio Ghibli movies.

items.title: Well, the Greek Prime Minister Seems Happy With The Odyssey — He Called Christopher Nolan to Thank Him for 'Stimulating Global Interest in Ancient Greek Culture'
items.description: The Greek prime minister called Christpher Nolan to personally congratulate him for The Odyssey, which he said has boosted interest in ancient Greek culture.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The Greek prime minister called Christpher Nolan to personally congratulate him for The Odyssey, which he said has boosted interest in ancient Greek culture.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis spoke to Nolan on Monday afternoon via video call, congratulating him for his adaptation of the Homeric epic poem and thanking him for the film's contribution to “stimulating global interest in ancient Greek culture,” a press release from the PM’s office reads. The note added that “such productions bridge Greece's rich cultural heritage with contemporary creativity.”

Mitsotakis also spoke about The Odyssey’s huge box office success, and “expressed his appreciation for the fact that a significant part of the filming took place in Greece.” Parts of the movie were shot in the Peloponnese region of Greece, including Voidokilia Beach, the 13th-century Methoni Castle, the monolithic Acrocorinth overlooking the city of Corinth, Almyrolaka Beach, and Nestor’s Cave.

Mitsotakis’ conversation with Nolan comes hot on the heels of a scathing review of The Odyssey by Greek translator and University of Pennsylvania professor Emily Wilson, who called Nolan’s film a "confused" and "abysmal" adaptation of Homer's text.

The Odyssey is a smash hit with critics and on course to make over $1 billion at the global box office, but some have questioned changes made by Nolan for his adaptation of Homer's epic poem.

Warning! Spoilers for The Odyssey follow:

Wilson, who is behind the 2017 translation of The Odyssey that Nolan reportedly credited with inspiring his take on the poem, has questioned the absence of the gods Zeus and Poseidon in the movie, and called the film’s anti-war and anti-cowardice message “incoherent.” She was also critical of Anne Hathaway’s Penelope, saying the role was so reduced it endangered “any possibility of believing in this marriage.” Neither did she like the scenes with Odysseus' dog, Argos, which she said “catered towards modern sentimentality.” Overall, Wilson said she thought Nolan “was trying to pack everything in while missing themes that were essential to the poem.”

In a recent interview with Time Magazine, Nolan explained some of his changes around Helen of Troy, Athena, and his new ending — although he still left much to audience interpretation.

Last week, Elon Musk claimed that Grok would make an AI movie of The Odyssey “that is historically accurate and true to the art of Homer,” by the end of 2026, although he did not make any claim about whether it would be any good.

Musk's comment came as little surprise, given the X and Tesla owner was a vocal critic of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in the run up to its release in theaters. Much of the online backlash, such as it is, revolved around conservative complaints that Nolan's The Odyssey would be “woke” for starring transgender actor Elliot Page (Sinon), rapper Travis Scott (the Bard), and black actress Lupita Nyong'o (Helen of Troy and her sister, Clytemnestra).

“This is a mythological story,” Nyong’o said in May. “I’m very supportive of Chris’ intention with it and with the version of this story that he is telling. Our cast is representative of the world. I’m not spending my time thinking of a defense. The criticism will exist whether I engage with it or not.”

She added: “It’s quite something to be a part of The Odyssey, because it is so grand. It spans worlds. So that’s why the cast is what it is. We’re occupying the epic narrative of our time.”

Ahead of release, The Odyssey was debated across the internet for its casting choices, some of its armor design, and the decision to have its characters speak with contemporary dialogue and in mostly modern American accents.

Prof Daniel Mendelsohn, whose translation of Homer's poem was published last year, said at the UK's Hay Festival in May that he was amused by "all of these bros suddenly worrying about Greek literature". According to a report in The Telegraph, Mendelsohn said: "What's so funny is that Helen has the tiniest role in The Odyssey… so the debate is particularly silly."

Image credit: Greek Prime Minister's office.

items.title: Fortnite Will Let You Unlock John Wick as a The Simpsons Character
items.description: Keanu Reeves has never guest starred on The Simpsons, but if he did, this is how his iconic assassin John Wick might look.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Keanu Reeves has never guest starred on The Simpsons, but if he did, this is how his iconic assassin John Wick might look.

Why has Wick been Simpson-fied? Well, of course, it's because he's the star of a new Fortnite update — specifically for its popular Reload spinoff mode. Players will be able to meet and unlock Wick for themselves (as long as they own the current battle pass) as they delve back into the game's excellent recreation of Springfield.

Fortnite first hosted The Simpsons' home town during a popular mini-season at the end of last year. Now, the map is back for the game's Reload offering, which grants players three lives and quick respawns before they're out completely.

With a match size of 50 players and Simpsons items, this sounds like it will recreate some of mayhem from last year's main battle royale offering. But there's a few new twists this time around, as well. Firstly, an area of the map will be dedicated to The Confidential, a neutral zone with passive healing.

Proximity chat is enabled inside The Confiditional, which could prove interesting (or incredibly annoying). Players can also choose to break the peace and begin firing, though at the penalty of being marked for all players, with higher-quality loot for the opponent who then takes you down. Is it worth the risk? Si vis pacem, para bellum.

Players who have been sticking with the main battle royale mode's compulsive Sprite collecting will likely be tempted to try Reload by the addition of an exclusive John Wick Sprite that can be extracted for use elsewhere (it reveals nearby enemies after knocking or eliminating an opponent).

Other changes to Reload will allow solo players to earn additional reboots by damaging opponents. Finally, chests will restock over time — a first for the game. Tempted to drop in? John Wick will be joining Homer Simpson in Fortnite Reload tomorrow, Thursday July 30, with around three weeks to unlock him for yourself.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

items.title: How 97 Copies of an Unreleased Version of Super Mario Bros. Duck Hunt Were Discovered in a Wisconsin Warehouse
items.description: When Jason Ganos was asked to help sell an old box full of NES cartridges, he figured they would be pre-owned copies of games that had already been circulated in the market. He had no idea that he was about to make a historic discovery that would change his life forever.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
When Jason Ganos was asked to help sell an old box full of NES cartridges, he figured they would be pre-owned copies of games that had already been circulated in the market. He had no idea that he was about to make a historic discovery that would change his life forever.

Waukesha, Wisconsin is a suburb of the greater Milwaukee metropolitan area that boasts around 71,000 people. Its downtown center looks like it jumped straight out of the '50s, packed with old-fashioned soda shops, classic burger joints, and antique stores.

One of these stores is a vintage collectibles shop called OneStopWonders, owned by collector Kevin Braun. It’s got everything from VHS tapes, retro games, vintage clothes, and anything else a nostalgic Gen X / Millennial could want. Jason Ganos, owner of the website NintendoWire and an avid Nintendo fan, began working with Braun three months ago, initially helping him repair old pinball machines.

After learning of Ganos’ website, Braun asked him if he’d be willing to help him sell some video games that had been languishing in his stock. At first, these were fairly normal titles for the PlayStation, GameCube, and Super Nintendo — but then Braun hit him with a doozy.

According to the shop owner, a seller came into his store with a box of NES cartridges six years ago. These had somehow ended up with the seller’s grandfather, who supposedly worked for a precious metal recovery service. The seller claimed that Nintendo had wanted to get rid of its stock quickly, and rather than dumping the cartridges, sold them to the recovery service for a small sum, allowing the service to extract gold from the circuit boards.

Speaking to IGN, Ganos admitted that he found the tale a bit fantastical — but it wasn’t nearly as wild as what was actually in the box.

The rectangular box, outfitted with three stickers with both English and Japanese text, had been sitting in Braun’s storage unit collecting dust for the last six years. One of the box’s stickers said that it had been shipped on December 1, 1995, while another revealed what was stored inside: 100 pcs of Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt for the NES.

This came as a surprise to Ganos, who noted that Duck Hunt was a pack-in game that came with a purchase of an NES console. By December 1995, the NES was already fairly late into its life cycle, making things even stranger.

Inside the box were 97 individually-wrapped copies of Super Mario Bros. / Duck Hunt with a manual on the back of each cart. There’s no telling where the other three copies went, but Ganos was initially convinced that they couldn’t be very valuable, given that Duck Hunt was one of the most widely-distributed games for the NES. However, he was quickly proven wrong after uploading photos of the haul to a collector Facebook group, which he swiftly deleted after learning just how mind-blowing his discovery really was.

Ganos says that he was approached by a director of one of the world’s biggest grading companies, as well as a director of PSA Games, who both warned him that something “seemed off” about the carts and asked him to take extensive photos of the inside of one of the games, circuit boards and all.

“They both told me the same thing: ‘These are either fake, or these are brand-new, never-before-seen variants of these games,’” he told us. “Like, the back label is different. The manual has different language in the back. There’s different dates listed in the back of the manual. The motherboard is completely different. There’s text on the motherboard that is not on any known copies of Super Mario Bros. Duck Hunt.”

Judging by what they could see on the manual, these copies of Duck Hunt were manufactured in late 1993, making them the latest prints of the game that have ever been seen thus far. Naturally, this one-of-a-kind find drew lots of attention on the Facebook group, prompting him to take down the post and immediately contact PSA for authentication.

Mere hours later, Ganos was on a plane to California with a suitcase packed with all 97 cartridges, terrified they’d get confiscated by TSA or worse, dismantled by the agency. Luckily, that didn’t happen, and PSA was able to confirm that all 97 copies were totally legit. Not only that, but five of them were perfect 10s — a number that PSA had never given to an NES cartridge before. (The total breakdown is: 60 9.8s, 31 9.6s, five 10s, and one 9.4.)

Speaking with IGN, Head of PSA Video Games, Claire Shelton, described her thoughts after seeing the cartridges for herself.

“We were shocked,” she told us. “It almost felt too good to be true. We’ve looked at so many examples over the years. Our graders have graded hundreds of thousands of examples across all platforms, and it’s often the case with tens where you almost start doubting yourself. You’re like, ‘I must be missing something. There’s no way it could be perfect.’

“We look at so many things, and everything has at least some flaws, so for these to be as good as they were… we’re looking for perfection, or at least as close to it as you can come. Because with injection-molded parts, there’s always going to be pulloff lines right from where something is detached from a mold, or just the intricacies of manufacturing are going to leave things with a little bit of inconsistency. We were very grateful to be able to identify four of these that met that standard.”

The haul was so special that PSA serialized the entire collection, encapsulating each copy along with its manual, something the company has never done before.

But what makes these copies so special? The fact they were unopened straight from the manufacturer, that they were a new variant with a manual on the back of each cart, and that they boasted a bilingual back label," Shelton explained.

“There just aren’t very many of those, and for Nintendo to have gone out of its way to create a new variant for whatever reason, then presumably not letting any of those see the light of day… it would be pretty unusual for Nintendo to do a new sticker variant for literally 100 copies. You’d typically expect that number to be much, much higher, like into the thousands for revisions, especially for a game like Mario / Duck Hunt, which had many millions of copies sold in its lifetime,” she told us.

However, the MVP of these copies’ pristine condition wasn’t Braun’s temperature-controlled storage unit; Shelton said that if it hadn’t been for the plastic baggies that each cartridge was stored in, they would have most certainly been in worse shape.

“Even without movement, dust can cause scratches and micro-wear over time. If these had not been bagged, I feel confident saying that there would not have been any tens. Those bags did a whole lot of work,” she said.

Now, for the big question: What’s the dollar amount of these cartridges’ value? Shelton admitted that she couldn’t say for certain, but speculated they could land somewhere in the four-to-five-figure range.

“Four digits would be the floor,” she told us. “Multiple thousands of dollars, for sure. Given that the public will be able to ascertain that the 10 rate was roughly 4%, I think it could easily be in the five digits. I wouldn’t expect it to exceed the five digits, but I’ve been surprised before and I’d love to be surprised here. I do think this is the kind of thing that, given the novelty and if you’re a betting person, I wouldn’t expect more of these to show up, and the odds that they’re gonna be in better condition than these is also quite unlikely.”

On August 12, three of these cartriges will go up for auction through Goldin Auctions. The auction will run for three weeks, ending tentatively on September 9. Ganos told us that he would also like to auction one of the carts off for charity, though no concrete plans for this have been set in place just yet.

“It feels completely surreal that this happened,” Ganos admitted. “I think it makes it even more surreal that I happened to live in this tiny little small town, with this tiny little downtown area, with a tiny little retro shop, and I ended up making friends with the guy who had this thing in storage for six years.

“Nintendo has been a part of my life for as long as I can remember. And Mario Brothers Duck Hunt is the very first video game I ever remember playing, so it’s surreal and it’s fantastical, and I’m just happy that this all fell on my lap. It just feels really cool to be part of this type of Nintendo history.”

Image Credits: PSA, Jason Ganos

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

Now, for the big question: What’s the dollar amount of these cartridges’ value? Shelton admitted that she couldn’t say for certain, but speculated they could land somewhere in the four-to-five-figure range.

“Four digits would be the floor,” she told us. “Multiple thousands of dollars, for sure. It just feels really cool to be part of this type of Nintendo history.”

items.title: 5 Years Later, Cool Cyberpunk Shooter The Ascent Is Getting a Major Update — and It Sounds Like a Sequel Is in the Works
items.description: The Ascent is set for a surprise major update to coincide with the game’s fifth anniversary — and it sounds like a sequel is on the way.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The Ascent is set for a surprise major update to coincide with the game’s fifth anniversary — and it sounds like a sequel is on the way.

Neon Giant’s twin-stick action RPG impressed players upon its 2021 release for its punchy action, highly detailed environments, and beautiful cyberpunk aesthetic. In IGN’s The Ascent review, we said, “The Ascent’s satisfying gun-tastic action-RPG gameplay loop mixes with its beautiful cyberpunk aesthetic to create an overall enjoyable experience. Neither its story nor its characters are all that memorable, and its enemy encounters can stumble toward the end, but its gunplay and ultra-violence in a neon-soaked world combine to craft a co-op-friendly game you don’t see every day.”

Now, publisher Krafton has announced that the upcoming update, due out in November 2026, will bring “a smoother more dependable experience for solo and co-op players, including improvements to co-op teleportation, the encounter system, save-game reliability and player-progression reliability.”

And then this interesting note:

“Final details will be shared closer to release alongside plans to expand The Ascent across new platforms, genres and future sequels. “

That to me sounds a lot like The Ascent 2 is in the works, and perhaps a Nintendo Switch 2 version of The Ascent is coming. But the mention of new genres is interesting, too. Could a full-blown first-person action RPG The Ascent game be a possibility? Given The Ascent has had over 12 million players, perhaps news of a sequel shouldn’t come as a surprise.

“We are incredibly proud of what we built with The Ascent and grateful to the millions of players who have made the journey to Veles,” said Arcade Berg, co-founder of Neon Giant. “We have also listened closely to feedback about where the experience can be stronger. With Krafton’s support, this update marks a new chapter for the game and for our ambitions for The Ascent as a franchise.”

Swedish studio Neon Giant is made up of only 20 developers, but it has a lot on its plate. Not only is it working on this The Ascent update as well as whatever’s next for the franchise, but it’s developing the promising No Law, which looks a bit like Cyberpunk 2077. I recently interviewed the team about how it’s developing No Law, which has a number of really exciting features open world fans will be keen to hear about.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

items.title: Pokémon Pokopia Expansion and Free Update Arrive Next Week, Unlocking Underwater Gameplay
items.description: Pokémon Pokopia will unlock underwater gameplay next week as part of a free update, alongside the launch of the game's first expansion.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Pokémon Pokopia will unlock underwater gameplay next week as part of a free update, alongside the launch of the game's first expansion.

On August 5, all players will gain the new Dive ability from a passing Manaphy, the Mythical water creature (that Pokémon Go seems to have forgotten exists). With Dive unlocked, you'll be able to summon up a bubble of air around your head — finally allowing your Ditto avatar the ability to survive for longer than a few seconds below the waves.

Indeed, underwater gameplay will allow you to build beneath the sea just as you currently can on land. Meanwhile, your gathered Pokémon can swim along with you.

Take a deep breath and unwind as we go on a deep dive into the underwater town of Bubbly Basin. 🫧🤿 The #PokemonPokopia Expansion Pass paid DLC Part 1: Bubbly Basin releases August 5, 2026. pic.twitter.com/iJPgzteM0P

— Pokémon (@Pokemon) July 29, 2026

All of this ties into the arrival of Pokopia's first paid expansion, Bubbly Basin, which will also become accessible on August 5 to anyone with the $34.99 Pokémon Pokopia expansion pass.

Most notably, this expansion adds the game's first post-launch region, the aforementioned Bubbly Basin, which features swathes of submerged land for you to flex your new Dive abilities. It's here you'll also meet Popplio, Mudkip, Corsola, Corphish and Chinchou, who'll teach you how to plant underwater grass, grow underwater watermelons, and power underwater electronic items (which sounds dangerous).

Other Bubbly Basin Pokémon spotted in today's trailer include Buizel, Lumineon, Stunfisk, Frillish, Carvanha, Sharpedo, Lantern, Totodile, Primarina, Golispod, and Dhelmise.

As you might expect, the expansion adds fresh items and furniture to collect, plus a Sharpedo submarine base. Finally, Bubbly Basin holds more secrets in its deepest depths: dark underwater caves illuminated only with neon coral.

You can purchase the Pokémon Pokopia expansion pass now ahead of Bubbly Basin's launch next week. The pass also includes a second expansion due this year that will add accessories for your Pokémon to wear, and a third expansion due in 2027 that adds yet another town.

Image source: YouTube

items.title: 'Without His Help, Spike Wouldn't Would Have Lasted': Buffy Star James Marsters Says His Attempts at a British Accent Were Saved by Giles Actor Anthony Head
items.description: Buffy star James Marsters has said that Spike would not have survived long without some behind-the-scenes British accent tutoring from Giles actor Anthony Head.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Buffy the Vampire Slayer star James Marsters has said that his fan-favorite character Spike would not have survived long without some behind-the-scenes tutoring from Giles actor Anthony Head.

Marsters played British vampire Spike from the show's second season onwards, and famously was so popular that he was upgraded from a guest star to a full-on regular. But Marsters has now revealed that his initially-dodgy British accent would have likely cut his time on the show short, if natural born Brit Anthony Head had not intervened.

Head passed away last month aged 72, due to complications from pneumonia. The beloved actor also starred in Little Britain, Merlin, and Ted Lasso, but remains best known for his quiet presence as Rupert Giles throughout Buffy's seven seasons.

"I remember early in Season 2, my accent wasn't that great," Marsters said at a recent convention, via MonopolyEvents. "In the script they had me say 'bullocks' and it was written by an American, so it was spelled 'bullocks.' So I did what I was told and said 'bullocks.' [Note: British people say "bollocks."]

"He came up to me and goes, 'We don't say it like that, you prat. You're embarassing me back home, so I'm going to help you now.' And he tutored me by force. He would come at lunch when the new script came out, he wouldn't even knock, and we he would just come in and we'd go through my lines line-by-line until he was satisfied I wouldn't embarass him anymore.

"I swear, without his help, I don't think the character would have lasted. And frankly, I think he was the best actor on Buffy, and the best human. He was always patient, always kind, he was our rock."

Head's death was marked by an outpouring of grief from fans of the series, as well as many of his former co-stars, who have variously spoken of his acting ability and presence on set. His passing follows the recent deaths of two other Buffy the Vampire Slayer regulars over the past year: Xander actor Nicholas Brendon, who passed away earlier this year aged 54, and the loss of Dawn actress Michelle Trachtenberg last year, aged just 39.

Earlier this year, fan hopes of a Buffy continuation series were dashed when Hulu decided to pass on the project, following a lengthy development and the shooting of a pilot episode last summer.

Image credit: Albert L. Ortega/WireImage.

items.title: The Balrog vs Sauron Fight Is Either Blasphemy or Awesome, Depending on Where You Stand on The Lord of the Rings Adaptations
items.description: The Balrog vs Sauron fight is either blasphemy or awesome, depending on where you stand on The Lord of the Rings adaptations.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
One of the big stories coming out of San Diego Comic Con 2026 was that the Balrog in Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power not only speaks, but fights the Dark Lord himself, Sauron.

Simon Pegg plays the Balrog, famous for his battle with Gandalf in The Fellowship of the Rings. In Season 3 of The Rings of Power, Sauron confronts the Balrog, seeking the power to forge the One Ring. They have a fight, which, as we see in the video below, sees Sauron use the Crown of Morgoth to deflect the Balrog’s flame sword attack. The video does not include the Balrog speaking, but we do get a hint at a line of its dialogue via a prompter that Pegg uses to provide voice over. "Crawl back to your world above," the Balrog will say.

None of this is in any Middle-earth-related text J. R. R. Tolkien wrote, of course. In no book did Sauron either meet the Balrog — or any Balrog for that matter — nor did the Balrog speak. Neither did Tolkien’s work include Sauron wielding the Crown of Morgoth like a shield. He never even had it to begin with.

The Rings of Power has form when it comes to deviating from the source material, so anyone who watched the first two series of the Amazon show probably won’t be surprised to hear the Balrog talk. I’ve been keeping a close eye on reaction from The Lord of the Rings fans to see what they think of this latest — and probably most surprising so far — deviation from Tolkien’s work. From what I’ve seen there are two reactions: disgust and excitement.

Let’s start with the excitement. There are a lot of people who think the clip we see of Sauron fighting the Balrog looks awesome, and they can’t wait to see more. They don’t care if it never happened in one of Tolkien’s books, they’re just looking forward to some cool TV set in the Lord of the Rings universe. And there are also some big fans of The Lord of the Rings lore who are perfectly fine with how this is all going down, and feel it makes sense within the canon established by Tolkien himself.

The Nerd of the Rings, for example, said “this shot goes so hard,” in a tweet about the Sauron versus Balrog fight. “While this is original to the show (Sauron & Durin’s Bane face to face) I give them a lot of credit for playing w/ something countless fans have asked: ‘why doesn’t Sauron team up with the Balrog?’

“For the record there’s no reason a balrog can’t speak.”

That’s a somewhat surprising take from The Nerd of the Rings, who has one of the largest Lord of the Rings YouTube channels around and is known for comprehensive lore videos. But I think it’s also an interesting one. This is someone you’d expect to be first in line to point to Tolkien’s books and say 'it never happened!,' but they're excited to see it nonetheless.

I’ve also seen people insist this encounter actually could have happened in the lore. While Tolkien didn’t create these scenes, their existence in the show doesn’t necessarily override the lore he has established. The Rings of Power is set in the Second Age, thousands of years before the events of The Hobbit. It is an age that wasn’t explored much by Tolkien, so there is plenty of room for new ideas. Who’s to say Sauron didn’t learn how to forge the One Ring from the Balrog? Who’s to say the Balrog didn’t speak when he wasn’t being disturbed by annoying dwarves? Not Tolkien, who didn't say much at all about the Second Age.

I’m playing devil’s advocate to a degree here, because it must be said that there is a lot of push back on what The Rings of Power is doing with the Balrog and Sauron in Season 3. There is a vociferous debate about whether the Balrog or a Balrog (we’re still not sure if this Season 3 Balrog is the Balrog from Season 2 or from The Fellowship of the Ring) should be able to speak. Some are pointing to a letter Tolkien wrote that rules out the possibility of the Balrog speaking, but this may relate to the scene on the bridge, specifically, rather than generally, or even in theory.

Should the Balrog even be active in the Second Age? Some think not, because it doesn’t make sense in the timeline Tolkien established. Durin's Bane is the name given to the Balrog that hid deep below the Dwarven kingdom of Khazad-dûm, the very same we see in The Fellowship of the Ring. Has Durin's Bane gone for a little walk to stretch his legs mid-hibernation? Even horrible monsters need to get away from their desk every now and then.

And how about comparing power sets? By pitting the Balrog against Sauron, The Rings of Power will make a call on how powerful the two beings are, which isn't something Tolkien ever did. Who would win in a fight between the Balrog and Sauron has been discussed by fans for years. Amazon is about to at least try to answer this question.

"This looks really cool, but a Balrog attacking Sauron? Both were Maiar. Both served Morgoth. Tolkien never had them fight," one critic of the scene said. "At this point, The Rings of Power feels like it's adapting itself more than it's adapting Tolkien."

"Except the Balrog and Sauron never met (canon)," added another critic. "And Morgoth’s crown was beat into a chain to imprison him at the end of the First Age (canon). The infantilisation and bastardisation of Tolkien’s source material to 'make mind blowing s**t' is utterly repugnant. It’s absolutely f***ing barbaric and a great insult to a man who toiled his entire life to give us these beautiful stories." Yes, people really care about this stuff!

My big question of Season 3 is whether it improves upon what’s gone before in terms of quality, after a couple of — in my opinion — rather disjointed seasons. Sauron is the best thing in Season 2, so I’m looking forward to seeing Charlie Vickers reprise the role — and do horribly evil things in the process, even to the Balrog. And if the Balrog speaking and fighting Sauron is upsetting for you, then you’re going to love the Nazgnagôl, which the showrunners have invented for Season 3.

Here’s the official blurb:

In Season 3, Middle-earth is at war. Five years have passed since the fall of Eregion. Sauron’s armies have marched across the whole of the world, conquering all in their path. Only a few isolated pockets stand between the Dark Lord and total victory — Khazad-dûm, where the Dwarves are now sealed deep within their mountain halls, and the elven realms of Lindon and Rivendell, which are protected by their Three Rings. But deep in the land of Mordor, in his newly completed tower of Barad-dûr, the Dark Lord toils day and night, obsessed with harnessing a power that will bring the last of his enemies to their knees: One Ring to rule them all... Now, all the free peoples of Middle-earth — Dwarves, Elves, Men, and Wizards alike — must find a way to come together, in a race against time to prevent Sauron from achieving his goal of utter domination of all life…

The first four episodes of Season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power will premiere on November 11, 2026. Episodes five and six will be available to stream on November 18, and the final two episodes of the season will be released on November 25.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

Now, all the free peoples of Middle-earth — Dwarves, Elves, Men, and Wizards alike — must find a way to come together, in a race against time to prevent Sauron from achieving his goal of utter domination of all life…
